fields.description_1:
Superfruitmand sells fruit boxes, baskets and gifts to both consumers and business buyers. Those shoppers may arrive with a different occasion in mind, such as a personal gift, an office order or a recurring business need. A product grid alone would not explain which category fits the moment or what happens after the choice.

The webshop therefore needed clear category routes, useful product details and a straightforward path into the cart without burying business information. Account features also had to support returning customers without becoming a barrier for a one-off order. On mobile, product cards and purchase actions needed to remain simple. The portfolio problem was to organise a gift-focused WooCommerce shop without inventing delivery, freshness or sales results that were not independently verified.
fields.description_2:
I organised Superfruitmand around the reason for buying as well as the product itself. Fruit boxes, baskets, gifts and business options each have a clear place, while product pages provide the detail needed before adding an item to the cart. Business information stays accessible without interrupting customers who only want to place a personal order.

Account functions support repeat use, but the shopping path does not depend on them. On mobile, categories, product choices and cart actions keep a predictable order so the main purchase task stays visible. The portfolio case now describes how WooCommerce supports several fruit-gifting situations under one store, while avoiding unsupported claims about delivery speed, product freshness, repeat purchase rates or commercial performance.

fields.description_1:
Progress has to support two recruitment audiences without making either one search through the other's information. Job seekers want vacancies, role details and a clear application path, while employers need staffing services, sector knowledge and enough trust to start a hiring conversation. Reviews can help both audiences, but they do not answer the same questions.

The website therefore needed separate candidate and employer routes with context only where it is useful. Vacancy discovery had to remain quick on mobile, while employer pages needed room to explain the service without competing with job listings. The portfolio story also had to avoid claiming faster placements, more applications or better hiring results without evidence. The challenge was to keep one recruitment brand coherent while serving two distinct decisions.
fields.description_2:
I structured Progress around a clear choice between finding work and finding people. Candidates can move from vacancies to role information and application actions without being interrupted by employer sales content. Employers can review staffing support, sector expertise and relevant proof before opening a conversation about a vacancy or workforce need.

Reviews and shared company information support both routes but do not replace the audience-specific content. On smaller screens, vacancy cards, application actions and employer contact routes keep separate priorities. I used direct labels so visitors understand the next step without learning internal recruitment terminology. The portfolio case now explains how WordPress supports both sides of a staffing business without making unsupported claims about placement speed, candidate volume, retention or commercial growth.

fields.description_1:
Bedrijfsboekhouder offers online accounting support to entrepreneurs who may need bookkeeping, tax returns, annual accounts, payroll help or financial guidance. These services often connect, but a visitor should not have to understand accounting terminology before finding the right starting point. A long list of tasks would make the offer feel more complex than necessary.

The website needed to separate administration from specialist financial work and show when an appointment is the useful next step. Pricing or service information had to remain clear without implying a guaranteed saving or tax outcome. Mobile visitors also need to reach the relevant route quickly. The portfolio problem was to make an online accounting service understandable and credible without relying on jargon, vague expertise claims or unverified financial results.
fields.description_2:
I organised Bedrijfsboekhouder around recognizable business needs instead of internal accounting categories. Bookkeeping, tax work, annual accounts and payroll support each have a clear route, with supporting details placed where they help an entrepreneur understand what comes next. Appointment actions appear after enough context for a useful financial conversation.

That structure keeps routine administration easy to find while leaving room for more specific questions. I used plain wording and avoided promises about tax savings, profit or compliance outcomes that depend on the client's records and circumstances. On mobile, service choices and appointment actions remain easy to scan. The portfolio case now reflects the actual online accounting workflow rather than presenting the project as a generic financial-services website.

fields.description_1:
Prometaal works with recyclable materials, collection and logistics for business customers, so the first question is often operational: what material is involved and how should it be handled? Sustainability information matters, but it cannot replace details about collection, transport or the type of recycling service a company needs.

The website therefore had to make materials and logistics understandable before pushing visitors toward an enquiry. Different business situations needed routes without implying that every material or load follows the same process. Mobile users also need to identify the relevant service without scanning long industrial descriptions. The portfolio story had to stay factual and avoid unverified claims about recycling percentages, environmental savings or turnaround times. The challenge was to connect material knowledge with a usable business-service journey.
fields.description_2:
I structured Prometaal around the material and service questions that business customers are likely to know first. Recyclable materials, collection and logistics each have a clear place, while sustainability context supports the process instead of becoming the only message. Visitors can understand the relevant route before describing quantities, locations or other details in an enquiry.

Supporting information stays close to the material or service it explains, and the mobile layout keeps those choices readable without dense industrial copy. I avoided broad claims about circularity or environmental impact that were not backed by project evidence. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress presents an operational recycling business: identify the material, understand the service and then start a practical conversation about collection or logistics.

fields.description_1:
Blenco sells made-to-measure window decoration, which means customers cannot simply choose a product and add a standard quantity to the cart. Product type, fabric or style, colour, measurements and mounting choices all affect what is being ordered. If those decisions appear at once, the product page can become difficult to understand, especially on a phone.

The webshop therefore needed a configuration flow that introduces choices in an order and keeps price and cart actions connected to the selected options. Guidance had to help customers measure or choose without suggesting that every installation is identical. The portfolio story also needed to avoid claims about fit or installation results beyond the actual configuration. The challenge was to turn custom window decoration into a manageable WooCommerce buying journey.
fields.description_2:
I structured Blenco so customers configure a made-to-measure product step by step instead of confronting every option at once. Product type and visual choices come first, followed by colour, measurements and mounting preferences. The cart action remains tied to the completed configuration so the order reflects the choices the customer actually made.

Helpful information sits beside the decision it supports rather than in a separate instruction page that is easy to miss. On mobile, selectors and actions keep enough spacing and a predictable order for custom input. The portfolio case now explains the ecommerce challenge behind made-to-measure window decoration, without claiming that every customer will measure perfectly or that the website itself guarantees installation, fit or sales outcomes.
